newsitem.title: POLAND: Budapest, Prague bourses hit new highs this week.
newsitem.headline: Budapest, Prague bourses hit new highs this week.

text.p: A new all-time high on the Budapest bourse and a new 1996 record by the Prague exchange overshadowed other East-European bourses this week.

The Central European Share Index (CESI) fell 1.17 percent this week to 1,513.64 points after hitting a new record on Monday. Zagreb gained but exchanges in Warsaw, Bulgaria, Bucharest, Bratislava fell.
BUDAPEST
The Budapest bourse was firmer this week and sharp rises by certain stocks pushed the BUX index to a new high on Monday.
The underlying trend remained bullish with strong corporate fundamentals, but analysts said investors were divided on the market's short-term outlook.

"(Domestic) small investors and speculators say that the shares are overvalued, while the institutional and foreign investors have a different opinion," said Tamas Revesz of Gog Securities, adding that the latter groups continued to buy.

All pharmaceutical stocks, home improvement products maker Graboplast and plastics firm Pannonplast hit new highs this week. Pannonplast last Friday announced the acqusition of Kaposplast, a step welcomed by analysts.
PRAGUE
The Prague Stock Exchange continued to post small gains this week, setting a new 1996 high of the PX50 index each day.
Late gains on Thursday by power company CEZ pushed the PX50 up 1.2 points to a 1996 high of 582.0 points, with the index up 4.6 points since last Friday's close.
Dealers said that only blue chip issues were attracting interest in the fairly thin market, as investors were looking elsewhere in the region.
WARSAW
Polish shares fell this week but analysts expected the correction, likely to be caused by profit-taking after 11.6 percent growth since mid-August, to end by early next week.

Analysts said the ruling left-wing coalition crisis, which followed the sacking of foreign trade minister Jacek Buchacz on Wednesday, could slow expected growth next week, but was unlikely to stop it unless the coalition collapsed.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell two percent from the last Friday's close to 13,657.4 points.
Analysts also said that next week the bourse might be influenced by investors speculating before the release of companies' August earnings reports.
BRATISLAVA
Bratislava shares saw another week of listless trading as the quiet summer season wound down, with the SAX index falling gradually and seen extending losses in the next few weeks.
The 12-share index fell over the week to Thursday's close of 212.94, from Monday's open at 221.79 points.
"Overall development at the bourse may be seen as unbalanced, and we expect the prevailing downward trend to continue over the next few weeks," said Jozef Cimra of ING Barings.
BUCHAREST
Shares traded mixed at the Bucharest bourse on Thursday, the week's second session, when turnover rose to 92.04 million lei, almost double the previous session's level.
Traders said they expected most prices to extend losses in the next few sessions as investors seemed to be in a profit-taking mood and sell orders were waiting to be matched.
BULGARIA

Only one stock -- Varna Grand Hotel -- traded on the Bulgarian stock market this week at a turnover of 9,170 levs ($43), pushing the 13-share Reuter All Bulgaria Stock Index (RABSI) down 41.07 points, or 0.24 percent, from last Thursday.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks traded mixed with blue chips forging ahead and traders said the current mild growth could continue in the near term.

Zagrebacka Banka ordinary shares gained 55 kuna from last Friday, closing at 730 kuna. Drugs firm Pliva rose by 600 kuna this week but did not trade on Thursday amid speculation that it might be included in free voucher distribution.
LJUBLJANA
In Ljubljana the SBI index fell 27.61 points, or 2.8 percent, to 954.81, and total turnover was at 303.9 million tolars ($2.3 million).
Bank UBK was the biggest loser, falling 40 percent, while preferred shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the top gainer, up 9.8 percent.
TIRANA
Neither treasury bills nor state bonds changed hands during the two weekly sessions of the four-month-old Tirana Stock Exchange on Monday and Thursday. SEPT 05 CLOSE WEEK'S CHANGE 1996 HIGH 1996 LOW
